image_description: A ringlet butterfly (Aphantopus hyperantus) resting on green grass blades with wings partially open, displaying brown wings with multiple small eyespots (ocelli) arranged in rows on both forewings and hindwings. The butterfly has a dark brown/black body, clubbed antennae, and visible legs gripping the grass. The background consists of out-of-focus green grass vegetation.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both antennae are clearly visible extending from the head, with distinct clubbed tips characteristic of butterflies.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The butterfly displays typical satyrid morphology with proportionate wings relative to body size, consistent with the 30-50mm wingspan range.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings uniformly brown to dark brown with small eyespots (ocelli) arranged in rows.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Wings are uniformly brown with clearly visible small eyespots arranged in rows on both forewings and hindwings, matching the diagnostic description.
